Zama Threat

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose the inner workings of the notorious Zama Zama's, and find out how organised crime syndicates run amok with impunity and pose a growing threat to society

Unique Selling Point:
We have never before seen footage of Zama activities, including the bombs they make to attack security underground, the weapons they have access to and the blatant way in which groups of 50 to 100 zamas are willing to attack mining operations, shoot guards, take hostages and operate without fear of police reaction. We also have the uncle of one of the two young members of the public who were shot next to the hi-way earlier this month, apparently by Zamas. Either the uncle Frikkie Kuhn the mother Joanna Kuhn of the murdered Jessica Kuhn will do an interview.

Summary:
Because there is still VAT allowed on second hand gold, there is an insatiable appetite for illegal gold which is legalised by being sold as secondhand jewellery. The scam fuels such a large market for illegal gold that amongst zamas some very organised, militaristic groupings, like the Ama Russians, Terini's en Matlamas have become violent, seemingly unstoppable forces, backed by millions of rand in cash, who are well armed and supplied. The problem is that some of that violence is now permeating ordinary society.

Further information:
Except for the footage showing the blatant violence zamas are willing to use against anyone who stands in their way, we have access to a zama and undercover agent who will tell us how commodities like food, tobacco and sex are sold underground to zamas who spend weeks or months below the surface. On certain operational gold mines a bowl of pap and vleis can be sold to zamas for R1500. We have footage and pics of the food, underground processing etc. WE HAVE ACCESS TO A SITE WHERE LITERALLY THOUSANDS OF ZAMAS OPERATE OPENLY. I DID NOT REALISE BUT THIS SITE IS PART OF THE SITE NEXT TO THE PUTTFONTEIN OFF RAMP WHERE THE YOUNGSTERS WERE SHOT. THERE IS A PART OF THE SITE WE WERE WARNED WE COULD NOT ENTER BECAUSE IT IS RUN BY BASOTHO'S WHO ARE VIOLENT. That part is next to Puttfontein off ramp. We are going to shoot with a drone and also speak to zamas from their off site.

Edward - (ZAMA ZAMA)

Mr. Waal De Waal Security Expert
Mr. Source "KANE" ILLEGAL GOLD BUYER

Zama Threat
12 June 2019

Voice
Over the years we’ve brought you many stories on zama-zamas, exposing the inner workings of South Africa’s notorious illegal miners.

Sound Up Chris Zulu
They are looking for a job, they can’t find a job. They thought this is much better, then to go to somebody’s house and to go and break(in).

Voice
Most zama’s are just illegal miners risking their lives to enter abandoned mines to make a living. But the lucrative industry, estimated to be worth billions off rands, has attracted organised crime syndicates who wage war against police, mine security and rival zama gangs.

Sound Up Chris Zulu
There’s a lot of fighting in this illegal mining, shooting, killing each other…

Voice
Carte Blanche has obtained footage, a lot of it which has never been seen on television before, which shows just how violent zamas can get. This leaked CCTV footage shows an operational gold mine in Gauteng being attacked by a large group of zamas in April this year. A security guard is shot several times and other employees are held at point blank range or savagely beaten. It’s a nationwide problem, and one that police seem unable to curb. Zama specialist Louis Nel says our mines are turning into war zones.

Sound Up Louis Nel
Derek: Have you seen some of the violence first hand?

Louis: Yes. There is people with tactical knowledge, military experience, they deploy observers, they’ve got snipers at certain positions, everything to protect them.

Voice
Explosives are obtained on the black market, while weapons are often bought or stolen from police and armed forces in South Africa and Lesotho. Waal de Waal of Bidvest Protea Coin says the violence is on the increase.

Sound Up Waal
About twenty years back there wasn’t any weapons involved, and these days you start getting R1 rifles, Uzi’s, automatic and semi-automatic weapons.

Voice
Even the supply of food is big business, as a zama working underground will pay inflated prices for goods, rather than risk surfacing and being caught by the authorities.

Sound Up Waal
These days you talk about a bread that costs R12 that costs R200.

Voice
Gauteng’s East Rand has become the scene of many violent zama incidents. This footage shows a shootout between security and armed zamas in the area. But along this stretch of the N12 highway between Benoni and Springs, the violence has spilled over onto our streets.

Link Derek
This is the Putfontein turnoff from the n12 near Benoni. It’s the crossroad between the squatter camp and the mines, and with the illegal mining, comes a trail of violence and bloodshed.


Voice
Many zamas who work the abandoned gold mines along the N12 highway live in the informal settlement adjacent to the off ramp. The zamas use the Putfontein bridge to access the multitude of old mining shafts directly opposite the highway, literally a few hundred meters away. Last month, the bridge was the scene of a terrible tragedy.

Link Derek
It was right here on the 26th of last month that a young couple were gunned down in cold blood after their bakkie ran out of fuel.

Voice
19 year old Johanco Fleischman and 24 year old Jessica Kuhn were on their way home to nearby Benoni when their vehicle ran out of fuel on the bridge. Crystal Park Community Policing Forum chairman Paul Raley was on scene shortly after the fatal shootings.

Sound Up Paul
Derek: You were on the scene shortly after the incident happened?

Paul: I found the vehicle standing on the side of the road, bonnet standing partly open, and the bodies of the two youngsters lying on the side of the road.

Voice
According to reports, Johanco and Jessica were waiting for a family member to bring them fuel when they were gunned down in cold blood by three men who had emerged from the side of the bridge. Investigators believe that the zamas in the area, many of them who travel with armed protection from rival gangs, were involved.

Sound Up Paul
Derek: How sure are you that Zama Zamas and their protection groups are involved?

Paul: Obviously the investigation is ongoing, there is no proof that it was zama zama’s, it’s an assumption that we all make purely because this area is dominated by the zama zamas and their problems. And if you look at past incidents, its a big problem.

Voice
Jessica Kuhn’s parents, Theuns and Johanna, have been left devastated by the tragic loss of the daughter they loved so much.

Sound Up Theuns and Johanna
Johanna: My children are my life. But my daughter… I just can’t believe she’s gone.

Voice
Jessica’s father Theuns says she was looking forward to starting a new career as a nursery school teacher.

Sound Up Theuns and Johanna Kuhn
Theuns: She was, she wanted so badly to have children, and teach children, it’s just heartbreaking for us to be here tonight and to say that our daughter is not with us tonight.




Voice
Private investigator Mike Bolhuis has been hired by the Fleischman family to look into the double murders. Two members of his team, former policeman Vince Harris and Werner Koekemoer were part of the investigation.


Sound Up Werner Koekemoer
There’s people doing protection work for them, that’s where the danger comes in.

Voice
Harris says they believe Johanco and Jessica were the victims of a tragic case of mistaken identity. He says the youngsters were probably mistaken for gold buyers or people who owed the zamas money.

Sound Up Vince Harris
Not so sure those who are in the mines itself, but the so called spotters or protectors, they are definitely involved.

Voice
It is a nation wide problem, with sites from Limpopo to the Free State, Mpumalanga and the North West under threat. Back in Gauteng we found more trouble on the West Rand,where a group of zamas had occupied the Mintails Mogale Gold Mine near Krugersdorp. When the mine was put into business rescue, it resulted in a zama free for all. Last week we accompanied a large police detachment during a tense stand off with armed zamas who had embedded themselves on a hill on the site.

Link Derek
The police say the zamas are still on the hill, we’re going to go with them in this Kaspir and just see what develops.

Voice
Earlier that day we had spotted some of the zamas on the hill seen here, but flushing them out at night with their high ground advantage proved to be an almost impossible task.

Link Derek
What we are seeing is just how difficult this is for the police, its a lethal game of cat and mouse. The zamas can be anywhere, in the bushes, in the mine shafts, in this equipment. It’s really a thankless task, and dangerous.

Voice
Back on the East Rand, Paul Raley told us the N12 bridge has become the dumping ground for dead zama bodies.

Sound Up Paul
The zama zama’s seem to have incidents with each other, they fight amongst themselves, people are killed. And very often the bodies are then brought up from the mine, they are dumped on the bridge. You can see just to our right there’s some sticks lying there, last week there was a zama zama brought up that was murdered and earlier this year we had one that was also brought up and what they did was they put a little note on his chest with the name and the telephone number for his next of kin.

Derek: And they’d been shot?

Paul: That’s correct, they’d been shot.


Voice
Much of the bloodshed here is blamed on zama rivalries, with one particularly fearsome group believed to operate from this hillside, within walking distance of the Putfontein bridge. Here they work the notorious abandoned Shaft 13. Frans van der Linde is a security specialist who does a lot of work for mines in the area.

Sound Up Frans
Derek: Frans it seems you don’t come out here unless you’re heavily armed?

Frans: Ja definitely, this is not a playground. We are approximately 400 to 500 meters away from the closest area to where they are now, so it’s a little bit safer here.

Derek: Am I being dramatic if I call this a war zone?

Frans: No, not at all. It’s definitely a war zone, we’ve had contact here. We’ve been attacked with hand grenades, Galil rifles, AK rifles, belt fed machine guns, all of the above ja.

Voice
Through some careful negotiation, we were able to access this large zama site adjacent to Shaft 13 and the N12.

Link Derek
This is the entrance to just one of the shafts on site. There are 11 shafts in total, and the zamas stay down there up to three weeks.

Voice
Like any large mine, the zamas underground are supported by a vast above ground operation, where everything from food and drink to a processing facility is available, at a price. A kilogram of zama gold can easily fetch R400 000 on the black market, fuelling the on going turf war on the east rand.

Link Derek
Well its just an amazing operation, everybody seems to have their own job, right now very peaceful, but you can see how shootings can break out between the different factions.

Sound Up Louis
The illegal miner as such, is quite a peaceful guy. You can talk to him he won’t do anything to you. The criminal actions around the illegal mining are being done by people that want to become the leaders. And they misuse their power through the barrel of a rifle - prostitution, murder, theft etc.

Voice
Over the past decades government has struggled to find a solution for the growing problem, and while plans were in the process to formalise the sector, nothing substantial has come of them yet. For now, the zamas are here to stay.

Sound Up Theuns
We don’t want any other person, or any other parent, to go through what we are going through. We want our roads safe and we want our children safe.
